steps.note: Pre-check: orders.amount exists, total does not, and nothing named orders_t is in the way.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='orders' AND column_name='amount') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.amount not found'; END IF; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='orders' AND column_name='total') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.total already exists'; END IF; IF to_regclass('public.orders_t') IS NOT NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'public.orders_t already exists'; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Rename in place (metadata only, no row rewrite) and put a compatibility view named orders in front of the table that exposes the column as both total and amount. It is a simple, automatically updatable view: old pods insert/read amount, new pods insert/read total, both hit the same base column, and base defaults (id sequence, created_at) still apply. All three DDLs commit together. The short lock_timeout and retry loop keep it from queueing app traffic behind a pending ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock while slow /customer scans hold the table.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE public.orders RENAME TO orders_t; ALTER TABLE public.orders_t RENAME COLUMN amount TO total; CREATE VIEW public.orders AS SELECT id, customer_id, total, total AS amount, status, email, created_at FROM public.orders_t; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 200 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders after % attempts', i; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Check the view answers under both column names.
steps.sql: SELECT id, amount, total FROM public.orders WHERE id = 1 AND amount = total;

steps.note: Roll the app over to the new column name. During the rolling update old pods use amount and new pods use total through the view.
Let terminating old pods drain (they keep serving ~3 s after SIGTERM, plus in-flight requests of up to 2 s).
Drop the compatibility view and give the table its name back, atomically, with the same lock_timeout and retry loop. From here on the amount column no longer exists anywhere.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOOP BEGIN DROP VIEW public.orders; ALTER TABLE public.orders_t RENAME TO orders; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 200 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders after % attempts', i; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Verify the end state: orders is a table, total is numeric(10,2) NOT NULL, amount is gone.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF (SELECT relkind FROM pg_class WHERE oid = 'public.orders'::regclass) <> 'r' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders is not a table'; END IF; IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND attname = 'total' AND NOT attisdropped AND attnotnull AND format_type(atttypid, atttypmod) = 'numeric(10,2)') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.total missing or wrong type/nullability'; END IF; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND attname = 'amount' AND NOT attisdropped) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.amount still exists'; END IF; END $$;
